correctness.rationale: For every dyadic L≥s≥2 the exact group-algebra substitution X=W+Y turns the dual update W=X+Y into multiplication by nilpotent W in the rank-s free B=F2[W]/(W^L) module. Reduction of a site monomial modulo W is Y^(i+j), a basis vector uniquely indexed by its diagonal class. Missing a class is an obstruction; meeting all classes supplies an s×s matrix invertible over B because its constant-term reduction is a permutation matrix. Time-shifts then span all Ls dual dimensions. Each class has L sites, giving the inclusion-exclusion formula. The random sensor threshold follows from explicit factorial moments and an error bound tending to zero uniformly over L≥s. A separate checker independently computes GF(2) observation ranks for all 65,808 sensor subsets on three small grids plus 640 seeded larger random cases; these are corroborative finite evidence only.

value.rationale: The object is a canonical deterministic 2D additive CA that destroys every initial configuration after a finite number of updates. Recovering its initial state before information disappears is a natural dynamical observability problem, not an arbitrary selected invariant. The theorem classifies all stationary sensor placements at once by a geometric diagonal-cover condition, proves the optimal size and observation time, gives an exact finite-size placement census for every sensor budget, and quantifies the large separation between optimal deterministic placement s and uniformly random placement s log s. This supplies a complete structural sensing result beyond routine statement of a rank test; the coupon-collector asymptotic is derived from the exact count rather than offered as an independent novelty claim.
